messages:
maria: Quick sync — profiler + prod traces show a recurring pattern where kernel selection prefers long-seq fast-paths and causes short requests to wait behind large KV-warmups. p99 for short sequences is spiking. Anyone else seeing this?

owen: yep, saw the same on canary yesterday. root cause looks like two things: the batcher coalesces by arrival time so long sequences often capture the slot and selected kernels are tuned for >512 tokens, which inflates scheduling.

jin: can we change matching strategy to prefer length-homogeneous microbatches? e.g., a quick-pass that groups <=128 tokens together and pushes long ones into a separate lane unless utilization drops.

maria: that's the basic idea. but we also need starvation prevention — short-tenants shouldn't be stuck when long inflight load is high. thinking: probabilistic admission that occasionally allows long into short lane to avoid starvation and refill credits.

owen: sketched a stochastic batcher that uses a per-lane token budget target. on admit: if short_lane.tokens + incoming.tokens <= short_target -> accept; else with prob p_accept = short_target/(short_lane.tokens + incoming.tokens) accept to avoid total blockade.

jin: interesting. what's the metric we measure to turn p_accept up/down? tail latency delta or starved-tenants count?

maria: both. primary control loop uses "starve_rate" (fraction of short requests queued > 50ms). secondary uses p95 delta. target starve_rate <= 0.02.

samir: ran a microbench this morning. baseline (master) with synthetic mix 70% short (<=64), 30% long(>1024):
```
baseline: p50_short=12ms p95_short=88ms p99_short=210ms
with-stochastic-v1: p50_short=13ms p95_short=42ms p99_short=95ms
long_p99 regressed by ~8ms though
```

kate: can you paste the perf flame data? curious whether kernel switch overhead is causing the long regress.

samir: attaching snippet from perf-bot: 
perf-bot: flamegraph: https://perf.internal/reports/26240/flame-merge.svg (summary: 35% in kv_warmup, 18% in matmul->gemm kernels, 12% in kernel-dispatch)

jin: kernel-dispatch overhead + KV warmups collude. idea: kernel matchmaking — before dispatch, compare incoming sequence length histogram with active batch; if mismatch > threshold, pick alternative kernel variant (fast short-path even if slightly suboptimal for long), but only for that microbatch. reduces dispatch churn.

maria: also propose per-tenant smoothing credits: each tenant gets a rolling token budget (windowed) with borrow/repay mechanics. borrow allows short tenants to pull a bounded amount when starved; repay happens when their traffic subsides. this prevents indefinite starvation when a tenant bursts.

owen: experiment plan:
1) implement stochastic admission (p_accept controller + metrics) behind feature flag.
2) add kernel-matchmaking switch that falls back to short-optimized kernel if mismatch ratio > 0.6.
3) per-tenant rolling budget with borrow cap = 2x baseline rate.
4) run canary on 10% infra with real-traffic replay.

maria: telemetry to collect: token_budget_usage, starve_rate_short, p95_short, p99_long, kernel_dispatch_count, kv_warmup_rate, throughput_tokens/s. alert if p99_short > baseline*1.3 or starve_rate > 0.05.

samir: note: watch KV cache hit distribution. previous fix (kv-warmup batching) reduced hits but increased warmup latency; this change might shift hit curves. include kv_hit_by_tenant and kv_warmup_count in dashboards.

kate: caution on rollout: the short-optimized kernel is lower accuracy for some quantized kernels we use — we need eval set check to ensure model outputs aren't regressing. add 5k prompt eval run in canary pipeline.

maria: good call. i'll add eval gate and a daily diff job. also adding deterministic seed runs to rule out nondeterminism from scheduling.

jin: one implementation nit — keep stochastic admission deterministic per request id for reproducibility in traces (hash(request_id) < threshold). that makes reproducing incidents easier.

nowen: (typo) owen: ack. i'll implement hashed prob. also adding a debug flag to log decision reasons for a tiny sample of requests.

perf-bot: profile job queued: perf-bot will post results to #perf-reports when finished.

maria: timeline: owen to prototype this week, jin + samir to run microbench on friday, canary early next week. if results look good we'll gate by eval and roll 10->50% over two days.

samir: tiny practical: in the microbench harness i used these commands to reproduce: 
```
# run synthetic mix
./bin/synth_load --mix short:70,long:30 --qps 300 --duration 600 --capture-traces
# collect nvprof-ish counters
nvprof --metrics inst_executed,dram_utilization ./bin/infer_worker
```

maria: perfect — keep notes here. if anyone hits surprising tail regressions, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
